content: Cefadroxil is a first-generation, semi-synthetic cephalosporin antibiotic that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis, thereby arresting bacterial growth. It exhibits bactericidal activity against rapidly growing organisms. This medication is used to treat a wide variety of bacterial infections and is effective only against bacterial infections, not viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Administration: Cefadroxil is taken orally, with or without food, as directed by a physician, usually once or twice daily. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each dose and measure the dose carefully using a proper measuring device or spoon. The dosage is determined based on the patient’s medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal efficacy, take the antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Drug Interactions: Antibiotics and Microbiota Oral Therapy: Antibacterial agents may reduce the efficacy of microbiota oral therapy. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. Cefadroxil and Mycophenolate: Cefadroxil increases the levels or effects of mycophenolate due to competition for renal tubular clearance. Monitor closely. Cefadroxil and NSAIDs (e.g., naproxen, nabumetone, oxaprozin, tolmetin): Cefadroxil may increase the levels or effects of these drugs through acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Cefadroxil and Aminoglycosides (e.g., neomycin, streptomycin, tobramycin, plazomicin): Co-administration may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefadroxil and Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (e.g., nivolumab, pembrolizumab, sintilimab, toripalimab): Cefadroxil may decrease the therapeutic effects of these agents through unspecified mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Cefadroxil and Live Bacterial Vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine): Cefadroxil may reduce the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is completed. Cefadroxil and Sodium Picosulfate: Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora required for drug activation. Monitor closely. Cefadroxil and Vitamins (e.g., pantothenic acid, pyridoxine, thiamine): Cefadroxil may decrease the levels or effects of these vitamins by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Cefadroxil and Warfarin: Cefadroxil may increase the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Side Effects: Common side effects include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, and urticaria. Rare but serious side effects include pseudomembranous colitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, anaphylaxis, increased transaminases, and neutropenia. Prolonged or repeated use may result in superinfection, such as oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Severe intestinal conditions caused by Clostridioides difficile may occur during or after treatment. Precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to cefadroxil, penicillins, or other cephalosporins. The suspension form may contain sugar; caution is advised for patients with diabetes or those requiring a sugar-restricted diet. Cefadroxil may interfere with live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, cefadroxil should only be used when clearly needed (Pregnancy Category B). It passes into breast milk, so caution is advised during lactation. Overdose: Symptoms of overdose may include severe gastrointestinal distress or central nervous system toxicity. In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention or contact a poison control center. Storage: Store capsules and tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Refrigerate the suspension and discard any unused portion after 14 days. Do not freeze. Important Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other infections unless directed by your doctor. Keep a list of all medications and supplements you are taking and share it with your healthcare provider to avoid potential interactions. Regular monitoring of kidney function and other lab tests may be necessary during treatment. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
